Ticket #25 — Webhook Event Processing

Difficulty: Medium

Practice Metadata

  • Interview format: Engineering ticket / existing-code debugging.
  • Primary skills: duplicate delivery, idempotency, observable state changes.
  • Expected duration: 50–60 minutes.
  • AI assistance: Allowed in guided practice mode for explanations, hypotheses, test ideas, and focused hints; the candidate owns and explains every change.
  • Candidate objective: Trace the reported behavior through the supplied code, state an invariant, make a focused change, and prove it with a regression test.
  • Interviewer evaluation: Problem decomposition, code navigation, root-cause explanation, incremental implementation, and test evidence. See the shared interviewer rubric.

Context

You maintain an order-status receiver for a delivery partner. A webhook is an incoming event notification; partners may retry it or deliver it late. Event IDs identify notifications globally. A sequence number orders updates within one order; monotonic history means applied sequence numbers only increase.

Practice report

Create order o1. Deliver event e2 at sequence 2 with status shipped, then a different event e1 at sequence 1 with status paid.

Observation after the delayed event Current starter Expected
Result for e1 applied stale
Current order status paid shipped
Applied-history sequences [2, 1] [2]

Both IDs must be remembered as processed, so retrying the stale notification returns duplicate without another state effect.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Validate nonempty event/order IDs, an integer sequence of at least 1 excluding booleans, and a supported status: created, paid, shipped, delivered, or cancelled. Malformed events are rejected without side effects. A new valid event ID for an unknown order is also rejected without side effects.
  • Apply a valid event ID at most once globally, including across different orders. A well-formed request using a processed ID returns duplicate without changing state.
  • For each order, apply only sequences strictly greater than its latest applied sequence. A new ID at a lower or equal sequence returns stale, preserving current status and history while remembering that ID as processed.
  • Applied events update status and append (sequence, event_id, status) to history. History is strictly increasing and status matches its highest sequence.
  • Different orders have independent sequence histories. Sequence ordering does not imply a new business rule restricting transitions between supported statuses.

Out of Scope

Keep the supplied route and repository. Partner authentication, network delivery, message queues, and a new order-status transition graph are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the delayed event, then test equal sequences under different IDs, exact retries, independent orders, and malformed requests. Assert status, applied history, and remembered IDs after each call, including a stale-event retry.
